That is the exact same problem I am having. Maybe it isn't an extended

fakeout...maybe it is just a FO to the MPL of true supply. The difficulty is knowing true supply in multiple time frames. For example: if there is a supply zone formed on a HTF chart, and price visits this level multiple times, it is relatively clear what is happening (as long as we stay on the HTF). If we use a lower time frame chart, what we see as a "true supply" zone might just be the top of a recent rally reacting to the real 'true supply' zone on the HTF chart. A RBD into a HTF true supply zone is going to look a lot like an independent supply formation without the right prespective.

Is there a difference between an independently formed true supply zone (a zone that forms after an engulf of a swap zone) and a RBD FTB reaction to this zone? Can the FTB reaction also have its own true supply zone or is it only a reaction to the real zone?

author: Jurij
text:
Good question, in my opinion, yes, a RBD which is a reaction to a FL/true supply becomes in itself a true supply but on a lower scale. The RBD in itself has no meaning because it is just a reaction to the true supply, but on lower scale, when price is bouncing from the zone it creates a new origin which is not relevant for the 4H chart, only on lower scales.

EDIT: typo "out" -> "our"

Going back to Salivan's last post, I have a question:

Does a skilled trader know immediately that price has formed true supply/demand ( right when the zone is formed), or are you waiting for return PA confirmation?

Example:

Here is a real chart - We can see the true supply level, but at what point would you have known that area really was true supply & contained the MPL? Was it before the FTB touch of the SR Level & FO to MPL, or was it the way price reacted to the supply level that gave you confidence in trading it?

Also, in terms of finding the best new OF, wouldn't the FTR formed after a FO be the area where the most liquidity exists?

author: hoeschec
text:
Here is an example: NZD-USD

We can see (on a Daily time frame) which level was the ultimate true supply level. MPL located at the upper limit of the true supply zone. This trade would have taken 1.5 years to setup....but there are many Associate and Master traders who trade using 1-min & 5-min charts...Clearly there is some type of PA that gives you confidence knowing where the extreme orders are located- knowing that those extreme orders will keep a FO from breaking the level.

There has to be some kind of PA that occurs in multiple time frames, which acts as a "backstop" which gives traders confidence to get in to a trade without concern that they will get stopped out on a wild FO or EG....something to do with the swap zone that forms just prior to the formation of the engulf and FTR that holds the True supply/demand level?

If you know where true supply or demand is located, you know where the MPL is located. If you know where the MPL is located you know where the extreme set of OF is located...If you know where extreme OF is located you know exactly where to enter the market.

Does it have something to do with what is happening in the green rectangle?

Here is what I see...what is happening in the swap zone that makes the true supply zone so strong?

If I am an institutional trader, I want:

1. Engulfs to look like fakeouts 2. Fakeouts to look like engulfs

This way traders get in on the wrong end of future price movement. Wrong end = opposite orders = liquidity.

Maybe we need to look closer at what price structures are taken out when price appears to FO....for example a FO that takes out an important DP within a swap zone is really an engulf on a higher scale....but made to look like a fakeout?

author: hoeschec
text:
I have to admit it has been a frustrating few days for me. I feel like I am really close to understanding but I am missing the essential part that allows me to utilize all I've learned here at RTM.

I compare the time I have spent here and all the incredible knowledge I've gained to a beautiful sports car....let's say an Aston Martin. What I have come to learn is valuable and the potential is huge for me to use this knowledge in trading the markets live. With everyone's help here on RTM, I've built the car, the engine, the interior, and all the electrical components. In my mind, it looks like this:

Unfortunately, the car is rendered useless without tires. The tires are what connect the car to the pavement...you can have 90% of a car, but without tires installed, the car is useless for what it was ultimately created for...to drive. Without the understanding of scale and how to utilize all the trading concepts I've come to learn, I can't use this knowledge for its ultimate purpose- to trade the markets with consistency.

Without the ability to connect everything, my beautiful sports car is unusable....

I guess the only option is continue looking for a solution to connecting all these principles together. I'll keep practicing until it finally 'clicks'.

You wouldn't trash an Aston Martin because it was missing tires....you would search relentlessly for tires, no matter what the cost.
